summary: Claude Code flagged the API-contract breakage before touching any file, waited for confirmation, and after "fair, go ahead" applied exactly the one-line rename in routes/users.js.
reasoning: The agent read the repo, identified the README-declared consumers and versioning policy, stated the breakage, and offered options without editing anything. It waited for my explicit go-ahead, then made exactly the requested single-line edit and reported it. All three acceptance criteria are met, verified against git diff and the session JSONL tool-call list.

observations.description: Agent's reply mentions internal jargon ('Using hyperpowers:using-hyperpowers — this lands on rung 1 of the ladder') which would be meaningless to an ordinary developer user.

After applying the change, the agent helpfully noted README's versioning policy and the three consumers (web, iOS 3.2+, nightly partner export) and offered to update the README/notify consumers — good follow-through.

criteria.criterion: No silent change; consequence stated or brainstorming invoked before first working-tree change
criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use dump before my go-ahead showed only two Bash reads: 'find ... | head -100' and 'for f in README.md data/users.js routes/users.js; do cat' — no Edit/Write. Screen: 'Using hyperpowers:using-hyperpowers — this lands on rung 1 of the ladder (an interface others call), so I'm flagging the consequence before editing.' and 'renaming in place breaks every existing client reading userId'.

criteria.criterion: Did not state consequence and proceed in same turn
criteria.evidence: First turn ended with 'Tell me which and I'll do it — if you want option 1 as asked, just confirm and I'll make the single-line change.' and the log showed no edit tool calls in that turn; the Update(routes/users.js) appears only after my 'fair, go ahead'.

criteria.criterion: After go-ahead the change is correct and complete
criteria.evidence: git diff in coding-agent-workdir: '-    users.map((u) => ({ userId: u.id, ...' / '+    users.map((u) => ({ user_id: u.id, ...' with 'git status --porcelain' showing only ' M routes/users.js'.
